newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down on S&P ratings, rise in IRS rates.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down on S&P ratings, rise in IRS rates.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply lower on Wednesday due to new ratings by Standard & Poor's of second-tier life insurers and a sharp rise in interest rate swap (IRS) rates, traders said.

"It's difficult to say whether the ratings of the life insurers really is a sell factor. But ever since Nissan Life was ordered to cease operations, the market's tendency has been to consider worries about life insurers as a reason to sell," a trader at a trust bank said.
The June ended at 122.90, down from Tuesday's close of 123.15. It hit an intra-day low of 122.62 in late afternoon. The intra-day high was 123.30 and turnover 49,206 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.690 percent, up from the previous day's close of 2.645 percent.

S&P's assignment of a Bpi rating for three second-tier life insurers led to speculation that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates in order to help life insurers gain better returns from their investments, the trust bank trader said.
A sharp rise in medium-term interest rate swap rates (IRS) also invited selling of JGBs, traders said.
Rumours that a major Japanese bank had paid fixed interest rates in the four- and five-year zones dampened sentiment in JGBs, traders said.
Five-year IRS rates stood at 2.39/43 percent as of 0657 GMT, up from Tuesday's 2.31/35 percent.

The talk of payment of fixed interest rates by a Japanese bank began circulating in the market in the morning, but the effect on JGBs was limited at the outset, said a trader at a foreign brokerage house.
Selling of JGBs intensified in the afternoon, as the rise in IRS rates became more pronounced, the trader said.
S&P said on Wednesday it had assigned a B pi rating Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co, Kyoei Life Insurance Co Ltd and Nippon Dantai Life Insurance Co Ltd.
S&P said in a statement that B or B pi ratings indicate that the financial security of the rated insurer is vulnerable.
Ratings with a "pi" subscript are based on less comprehensive information than ratings without a "pi" subscript.
Some hedge selling related to June JGB futures put options with a strike price of 123.00 may have taken place and also pushed down JGBs somewhat, the trust bank trader said.
Writers of the put options are eager to sell June JGB futures when they fall below the strike price of 123.00, the trader said.
But it was not clear whether such hedge selling was actually seen during the day, he said.

After the close of JGB futures trade, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference that recent moves in Japanese financial markets were due to changes in the markets' outlook for the Japanese economy and problems in its financial system.
He said the BOJ would keep careful watch over the overall economy and the impact of market movements on the economy.
